findings.title: A manual --post can turn a runner-pushed head green before its blind review has run
findings.why: mayPostSuccess allows success when a head has no blind-review status, which it treats as 'a PR made by hand'. But checkAndPush (scripts/agent-watch.mjs:394) posts only qodo-gate pending on each head it pushes. The blind-review status is posted only later, when continueRun sees Qodo's gate met. So between Qodo finishing and the runner's next poll, or for good if the run stops before that point (for example the reviewWaitMin timeout, an incomplete read or a crash), `node scripts/qodo-gate.mjs <pr> --post` posts qodo-gate success on a head that never had a blind review. That breaks the PR's claim that a blind review must pass before the gate goes green, and the code comment that a manual --post can't skip it. Fix: post blind-review pending on every head the runner pushes, or have mayPostSuccess refuse heads on agent/ branches that have no blind-review status.

findings.title: The Wisdom summary becomes proofs[0], so the first push's red-to-green proof is also posted as a duplicate comment
findings.why: publishPlan posts every proof after the first as a comment, assuming the first one is what the PR opened with. wisdomCheck now adds its summary to s.proofs before the first push, so the first red-to-green proof is proofs[1]. checkAndPush's publish() then posts it as a comment right after gh pr create, even though it is already in the PR description.

findings.title: statusesOf reads only the first page of statuses
findings.why: Rule 7 says list reads go through allPages. GitHub lists statuses newest first, so in practice the newest blind-review is on page 1. Still, it is a single-page GitHub read that the rule's review check names.

findings.title: The blind reviewer can still read Qodo's findings through the diff and git log
findings.why: BLIND denies reading .agent/review.md and similar files, but allows git diff, git log and git show. The work-ticket convention puts Qodo's findings into test names (for example "#107 7645d535: …") and commit subjects ("fix: Qodo's findings on #107: …"), so after round 1 the 'blind' reviewer sees Qodo's findings in the diff it is asked to review. The independence the gate claims holds only on the first review round.

findings.title: A blind finding with no severity blocks as a Medium but the status calls it an unreadable label
findings.why: blindVerdict treats a missing severity as serious. blockingWhy exempts blind findings only when f.severity is set, so a reproduced blind finding with no severity (no attribution_status, no action_level) is described as "1 with a label the gate can't read" in the qodo-gate status, not as a High or Medium.
